prerequisites: It is recommended to have passed Graphic Expression I and Graphic Expression II courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Know the methodology and design process of a 3D part or component on the computer.
Know the techniques of digitalization and model reconstruction by reverse engineering.
Be able to structure the design of an assembly and its 3D components so that its design is flexible and robust.
Be able to create 3D part models on a computer, using solid and surface modeling tools.
Be able to digitize and reconstruct models by reverse engineering.
Be able to assemble parts into assemblies considering the device's operation.
Be able to detect and correct functional errors of the different components in each device.
Be able to obtain assembly and exploded view drawings of devices designed in 3D on the computer, adhering to technical drawing standards.
Be able to perceive the options offered by mastering a high-level computer-aided design tool in other engineering disciplines.
Knowledge and abilities to apply graphic engineering techniques.

Ability to draft and develop projects in the field of mechanical engineering, for the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing processes.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to interpret technical projects and reports.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION TO DESIGN WITH HIGH-LEVEL CAD TOOLS
teaching_methods: Completion of assignments, reports, dissertations, and evaluation tests

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment of theory and CAD practicals
Assessment of the final project presentation
Assessment of the final project content

assessment_rules: A minimum score of 3.5 points is required for the continuous assessment of theory and CAD practicals. If this minimum is not met for the second call, the teaching staff will inform students about the activities/tests they must complete. The assessment consists of continuous assessment (30%), final project presentation (30%), and final project content (40%).
